sections.h2: How is Orchard Park laid out, and why does that matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Orchard Park is both a town and a village: the village sits inside the 38.52 square mile town, roughly 14 miles southeast of downtown Buffalo, so your first check is which of the two contains your lot. The area broke away from Hamburg in 1850 under the name Ellicott, became East Hamburgh within months, and received today's name on March 1, 1934 (Wikipedia).

Several hamlets lie within the town limits: Armor, Duells Corner, Ellicott, Loveland and Webster Corners. Highmark Stadium stands in the hamlet of Windom on the western edge, and Chestnut Ridge Park, the largest park in Erie County, fills the southern end. Drivers rely on US 219 along the west side, US 20 across the north and NY 277 and NY 240 near their junction with US 20.

School boundaries come up early in any showing. The Orchard Park Central School District runs four K-5 buildings named Eggert, Ellicott, South Davis and Windom, plus one middle school and one high school. Naming the correct elementary school in your listing saves buyers a round of questions.

sections.h2: How does Orchard Park look in the latest Census estimates?
sections.html:
QuickFacts puts the town at 29,804 people as of mid-2025, spread over 12,829 households. Owners live in 74.5 percent of homes, a typical owned home is valued at $360,700, and renters pay a median of $1,304 a month (Census Bureau).

  • Residents past 65: 24.5 percent of the population
  • Middle point for household income: $109,876 in 2024 dollars
  • Typical commute: 21.5 minutes
  • Density: 772.5 people on each square mile of land in 2020

Few owners relocate in a given year, since 91.6 percent of residents had not changed address over the previous twelve months. Owners pay a median of $2,323 a month with a mortgage and $910 without one.

sections.h2: Which Orchard Park offices handle permits, assessments and recording?
sections.html:
Four offices cover nearly every step of a sale.

  • Assessor's Office: keeps your assessment, takes informal review requests and receives grievance paperwork. Phone 716-662-6420.
  • Building Inspector and Code Enforcement: permits, inspections and zoning verification letters, from the Municipal Center on South Buffalo Street in the village. The counter is closed for lunch from 1 PM to 2 PM on weekdays.
  • Town Board: meets on the first and third Wednesdays of each month in the Municipal Building courtroom.
  • Erie County Clerk: records the deed and collects the transfer tax.

The town's home page also lists a presentation on rezoning around the stadium, dated February 25, 2026, and zoning map amendments dated October 7, 2026. A parcel near the stadium or along a corridor under study deserves a zoning verification letter from the building office before you commit to a price.

sections.h2: When can an Orchard Park owner contest an assessment?
sections.html:
Only during the spring window around Grievance Day, which the town sets on the fourth Tuesday of May. The Assessor's Office page lists the calendar below, along with a 1990 revaluation, a uniform level of assessment of 28.5 percent and 12,412 parcels.

Assessment stepOrchard Park date
Taxable status dateMarch 1
Valuation dateJuly 1 of the previous year
Tentative rollMay 1
Grievance DayFourth Tuesday of May
Final rollJuly 1

Source: Town of Orchard Park Assessor's Office.

At 28.5 percent, the assessed figure on a notice sits far below market value, and dividing it by 0.285 gives only a very rough full value. Hearing requests for 2026 had to arrive by May 19, hearings ran from 4 PM to 8 PM on May 26 in the Town Hall basement meeting room, and the town accepted nothing by email or upload. A complainant also supplied copies of Form RP-524 and backup documents for each of the five review board members. That day is over, so call the assessor for the 2027 schedule and read the assessment review page first.

A house inside the village may carry a second assessment. The state says villages that assess property take their own RP-524 complaints (tax.ny.gov), so ask whether yours does.

sections.h2: What does Erie County charge a seller at the deed stage?
sections.html:
An Orchard Park seller owes a combined state and county transfer tax of $4.50 on every $500 slice of the price, with a partial slice counted as a whole one. Albany takes $2.00 of that and Erie County takes $2.50, and the clerk collects it as the deed is handed in (Erie County Clerk).

A $360,000 price breaks into 720 slices, so the state share is $1,440, the county share is $1,800 and the bill is $3,240. Owners 62 or older who have lived in a one or two family house for a year or more can sign an affidavit, free at the clerk's office, that drops the rate to $2.00 per $500.

Recording is billed separately. On the clerk's residential deed schedule the statutory fee is $45, each written side of a page adds $5, Form TP-584 costs $10 and the RP-5217 transfer report costs $125, so a three-page deed totals $195. The additional 1 percent mansion tax starts at $1 million and the buyer pays it (tax.ny.gov).

sections.h2: What paperwork can slow an Orchard Park closing?
sections.html:
The big item is the state's seller questionnaire. Real Property Law 462 obliges the owner of a house with up to four units to sign it and hand it to the buyer ahead of the buyer's signature on the contract (statute). As-is wording in the contract stays legal. Several questions line up with local houses:

  • Do certificates of occupancy exist for the building?
  • Does water come from the municipal system or a well, and does waste go to a public sewer or a septic tank?
  • Has the lot had flooding, drainage trouble or water in the structure?
  • Which school district serves the address?

The building office says work begun before a permit is issued costs a double fee. Its permit list includes decks, fences, sheds, pools, roofing, furnace and air conditioning replacements, generators and added plumbing fixtures, and the town has asked for plumbing permits on all plumbing work since January 2020. Owners must also clear snow and ice from sidewalks beside their land. Close out or document any gap before an inspector or a buyer discovers it (building office).

sections.h2: When does a cash purchase suit an Orchard Park owner?
sections.html:
Paying cash removes the lender's appraisal and approval, so the remaining timeline is title work, state forms and recording. Owners weigh it when they would rather skip showings and repairs, as with an inherited house or a move that has a fixed date.

Whichever route you pick, gather the tax bill, permit records for past work and the Erie County deed details first. Get any offer in writing, settle who covers each closing charge, and let a New York attorney read the contract. The disclosure form, the transfer tax and any lien payoff stay on the seller's side of the table.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller cover Orchard Park's transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller covers it. Erie County's schedule totals $4.50 per $500 of price, split into $2.00 for the state and $2.50 for the county. Owners 62 or older who have lived in a one or two family house for a year can claim the reduced $2.00 rate.

faqs.q: Is a house that needs repairs sellable in Orchard Park?
faqs.a: Yes. State law lets both sides agree to an as-is sale. The owner still hands over the signed seller questionnaire before the buyer signs, so answer from what you know and attach any inspection reports you hold.

faqs.q: What date is Orchard Park's Grievance Day?
faqs.a: The town lists the fourth Tuesday of May. For 2026 that was May 26, so it is over and the next one lands in spring 2027. Call the Assessor's Office for the exact date, the appointment deadline and how many copies of the complaint form to bring.

faqs.q: What should I do about unpermitted work on my Orchard Park house?
faqs.a: Speak with the building office before you list. The town says work started without a permit costs a double fee, and the state questionnaire asks about certificates of occupancy. Closing out the permit, or disclosing the gap, is cheaper than reopening a contract later.

faqs.q: Which office records an Orchard Park deed?
faqs.a: The Erie County Clerk, the county's registrar of deeds. On the clerk's schedule a three-page residential deed costs $195 to record, and the transfer tax is paid in the same visit. Title companies and attorneys normally file for you.
